stem: Which of the following arteries is the terminal branch of the basilar artery:
fact: The posterior cerebral artery is the terminal branch of the basilar artery.
mnemonic: Basilar ends in PCA: posterior cerebral arteries.
finding: Source page displays posterior cerebral artery as the correct option; posterior-circulation anatomy corroborates the key.

stem: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by the ophthalmic artery.
mnemonic: Ophthalmic artery supplies the optic nerve in the orbit.
finding: Pages 1585–1586 reconcile as one question; page 1586 displays ophthalmic artery as correct and NCBI corroborates the supply.

stem: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The extracranial portion of the optic nerve is supplied by the ophthalmic artery.
mnemonic: Ophthalmic artery supplies the optic nerve in the orbit.
finding: This second OCR record is the answered continuation on page 1586; it displays ophthalmic artery as correct and NCBI corroborates the supply.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you likely to see in a lesion of the temporal optic radiation:
fact: A lesion of the temporal optic radiation will result in a contralateral homonymous superior quadrantanopia.
mnemonic: Meyer’s loop in the temporal lobe gives the upper field: pie in the sky.
finding: Source page displays contralateral homonymous superior quadrantanopia; NCBI localizes temporal Meyer-loop fibres to the superior visual field.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a typical cerebellar sign:
fact: An intention tremor is characteristic of cerebellar dysfunction. Resting tremor may be seen in Parkinsonism.
mnemonic: Cerebellar tremor appears with intention, not at rest.
finding: Source page displays resting tremor as correct and includes ataxia in the option list; the OCR draft lost that option.

stem: Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards side of lesion
Contralateral weakness of the face and arm
fact: Loss of two-point discrimination is most likely to occur in a lesion of the parietal lobe. Expressive dysphasia results from damage to Broca's area. Contralateral weakness of the face and arm results from damage to the primary motor cortex. Personality change results from damage to the prefrontal cortex. Conjugate eye deviation towards side of lesion results from damage to the frontal eye field.
mnemonic: Frontal plans, moves, speaks, and directs gaze; parietal discriminates touch.
finding: Source page displays loss of two-point discrimination as correct; PMC corroborates parietal cortical sensory loss.

stem: Regarding cerebrospinal fluid, which of the following statements is NOT correct:
options: The total volume of CSF is around 130 mL.
The bulk of CSF formation occurs in the lateral ventricles.
The inferior horn of the lateral ventricle projects into the temporal lobe.
The lateral ventricles are connected to the third ventricle by the cerebral aqueduct.
The fourth ventricle lies within the brainstem.
fact: The lateral ventricles are connected to the third ventricle by the interventricular foramen (of Monro).
mnemonic: Monro moves lateral to third; Sylvius moves third to fourth.
finding: Source page displays the cerebral-aqueduct statement as the incorrect option; NCBI confirms the lateral-to-third ventricular connection is via the interventricular foramen of Monro.

stem: The vertebral artery is a branch of which of the following blood vessels:
fact: The vertebral artery is a branch of the subclavian artery.
finding: Source page displays subclavian artery as correct; vertebrobasilar anatomy corroborates the key.

stem: The internal capsule primarily contains which types of white matter fibres:
fact: The internal capsule is a deep subcortical structure that contains a concentration of white matter projection fibres. Projection fibres connect the cerebral cortex with the lower part of the brain or brainstem and the spinal cord, in both directions.
mnemonic: Projection fibres project cortex to brainstem and cord.
finding: Source page displays projection fibres as correct and includes commissural fibres; NCBI confirms the internal capsule contains ascending and descending projection tracts.

stem: Damage to Broca's area will most likely result in which of the following clinical features:
fact: The Broca's speech area, in the frontal lobe of the dominant hemisphere, is the ‘expressive’ centre for the production of speech. It is connected to the Wernicke's speech area by the arcuate fasciculus. Damage to this area will result in an expressive dysphasia.
finding: Source page displays expressive dysphasia as correct; NCBI locates Broca area in the dominant inferior frontal gyrus and describes expressive aphasia after injury.
